Article Title: 'That's the world we live in': Travis Head breaks silence on wife's online abuse after Virat Kohli handshake row
Article Text:
Travis Head and Virat Kohli (ANI Photo)

Family affected by online abuse

NEW DELHI: Australia batter Travis Head has spoken publicly for the first time about the controversy involving Virat Kohli during the IPL 2026 match between Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) and Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB).The incident gained attention after cameras appeared to show RCB star Kohli skipping a handshake with SRH's Head after the game, leading to speculation about a rift between the two cricketers.Head, however, has dismissed the rumours, saying there was no issue to resolve."I don't think there's anything to patch over. That's just that's what it is. That's yeah. No surprises with how the competition went or what went on. So as expected," Head told Code Sports.The controversy took a personal turn when Head's wife, Jessica Davies, revealed she received abusive messages from fans on social media.Head admitted the online backlash was difficult, especially for his family, although he believes such attention is part of being a professional athlete."I think Jessica and I have a great perspective on things. That's the world we live in, and I think she's amazing in how she handles that kind of stuff.It was more the family stuff was built around it, flowing on to other family members who don't particularly see that sort of stuff," he said.Head also praised his wife for staying calm throughout the episode, adding, "Everyone forgets about it in a few days' time. She handled it extremely well. It's probably handling it with others and what other people's perspective of what things are like."Meanwhile, Kohli's Royal Challengers Bengaluru successfully defended their IPL title by defeating Gujarat Titans in the 2026 final in Ahmedabad.
Article Summary: Travis head speaks publicly for the first time about controversy involving virat kohli. Kohli skipped a handshake with srh's head after the game, leading to speculation about a rift. Head's wife, jessica davies, revealed she received abusive messages on social media.

Article Title: 'Why is he always retained?': Ashwin fires back at Mayank Yadav's critics
Article Text:
India's bowler Mayank Yadav (AP Photo/Wonder Mashura)

Mayank Yadav's return to international cricket could hardly have gone better, and former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin believes the young fast bowler deserves patience after overcoming a difficult spell with injuries.Playing his first international match since October 2024, Mayank announced his comeback in style during the opening T20I against Zimbabwe in Harare. The speedster was named Player of the Match after producing a match-winning spell that began with a wicket off the very first ball of the contest.Mayank removed Brian Bennett for a duck with a hard-length delivery that straightened after pitching, forcing an outside edge that was safely taken behind the stumps. He continued to test Zimbabwe's batters with his pace and discipline, dismissing Dion Myers during the powerplay to leave the hosts under immediate pressure. His spell laid the platform for India's commanding bowling display.The performance marked a significant moment in the pacer's career after an injury-plagued period stalled his rapid rise. Initially fast-tracked into the Indian side as part of the team's long-term plans for the 2026 T20 World Cup, Mayank spent the past two years battling recurring fitness issues that repeatedly interrupted his progress.Speaking on 'Ash ki Baat', Ashwin reflected on the challenges of returning from multiple injuries and urged fans to avoid judging players too quickly."It is not easy to go through a stress fracture at a young age. We often see and think, why is he always retained? He is always injured. We easily tell this. No player plays to get injured. Injury can be very painful. It is not just physical but also a mental barrier, especially if you are injured twice. It is not easy on the body. If it resurfaces, it plays on your mind. Mayank Yadav has a lot of time and is exceptionally talented. I want him to play more," he said on 'Ash ki Baat'.Ashwin also acknowledged India's convincing start to the series and congratulated new T20I captain Shreyas Iyer on securing his maiden victory as skipper."Congratulations to Shreyas for the first win. He would have been searching for it. There is not a lot to see when you restrict Zimbabwe to 120-odd. Mayank, Prince, and Ashok all got an opportunity," he said.Mayank's impressive return has not only revived India's pace options but also reinforced why he continues to be viewed as one of the country's most exciting fast-bowling prospects when fully fit.
Article Summary: Ravichandran ashwin believes mayank yadav deserves patience after overcoming a difficult spell with injuries. Mayank announced his comeback in style during the opening t20i against zimbabwe. The speedster was named player of the match after producing a match-winning spell that began with a wicket off the very first ball of the contest.

Article Title: Gautam Gambhir termed 'foolish' after ex-India selector's explosive Vaibhav Sooryavanshi verdict
Article Text:
Gautam Gambhir and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (Agency Image)

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi announced himself on the international stage in spectacular fashion during India's first T20I against Zimbabwe on Thursday, becoming the youngest player ever to score a maiden T20I half-century.The 15-year-old became the youngest player to score a maiden T20I half-century after racing to an 18-ball fifty in Harare. It was a timely response from the teenage batter, who had managed scores of 14, 13 and 15 in his first three appearances for India during the T20I series against England.Following those outings, Sooryavanshi was left out of the playing XI for the fifth and final T20I. His exclusion came amid intense scrutiny over India's selection decisions. Earlier in the England series, Sanju Samson , who had been India's Player of the Tournament during their T20 World Cup-winning campaign, was dropped from the side, with Sooryavanshi brought into the XI. However, for the fifth match, the management reversed course, restoring Samson and leaving out the youngster. Samson was subsequently omitted from India's squad for the Zimbabwe tour.Former India captain and ex-BCCI selector Krishnamachari Srikkanth admitted he was baffled by the decision to drop Sooryavanshi after only three failures and took aim at head coach Gautam Gambhir over the move."He (Sooryavanshi) has an effortless range of shots, yet, not one shot was cross-batted.This boy is really something special. How did Gautam Gambhir foolishly drop him, of all people, after three failures to crush his confidence?" said Srikkanth, speaking on his YouTube channel, as quoted by Sportskeeda.With Gambhir not accompanying the team on the Zimbabwe tour, former India batter VVS Laxman is serving as the side's interim head coach.Srikkanth also highlighted the youngster's commitment to improvement, revealing that Sooryavanshi immediately returned to work after the England series rather than taking a break."I salute Vaibhav for his dedication. After the England series, he didn't go home and instead went straight to the Rajasthan Royals camp. He has been working on his batting against the short ball because he wants to prove to the whole world that he is special," Srikkanth added.The 1983 World Cup winner was equally impressed by the fearless approach shown by Sooryavanshi despite the pressure of retaining his place in the national side. According to Srikkanth, many young players would have opted for a safer route after a string of low scores, but the teenager remained committed to his attacking game."The ease at which he scores at a 250 strike rate is extraordinary. Normally, after three failures, other players would have tried to safeguard their place in the Indian team by taking singles and twos. But he played fearlessly without worrying about the consequences. Scoring a 50 off 18 balls has become child's play for him. That's his greatness," Srikkanth elaborated.Sooryavanshi's explosive innings not only earned him a place in the record books but also strengthened his case as one of India's most exciting young batting talents. Srikkanth's comments also highlighted the selection dilemmas and team combination questions India continue to face.
Article Summary: Vaibhav sooryavanshi becomes youngest player to score a maiden t20i half-century. The 15-year-old scored an 18-ball fifty against zimbabwe on thursday. He had managed scores of 14, 13 and 15 in his first three appearances for india. Ex-bcci selector krishnamachari srikkanth has criticised gautam gambhir's decision.

Article Title: 'No question of retirement': BCCI rubbishes speculation over Rohit Sharma's future
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma (ANI Photo)

BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla has firmly rejected rumours over Rohit Sharma 's international future, stating there is "no question" of the India opener retiring at this stage despite growing speculation during the recent England tour.Questions over Rohit's future gathered pace after a prolonged lean patch with the bat, with reports suggesting the third ODI against England at Lord's could potentially be his final appearance for India. However, the 39-year-old answered those doubts in emphatic fashion by smashing 138 off 110 balls, becoming the first Indian batter to score an ODI century at the iconic venue.Speaking to reporters, Shukla rubbished the retirement rumours and insisted there was no truth to the speculation.“Rohit Sharma is a part of our team and is continuing to play. The things being circulated in the media and on social media have no meaning. As of now, there is no question of his retirement,” Shukla said.Rohit's century at Lord's also reinforced his own stance on his future. The India opener has consistently maintained that he wants to continue representing the country and remains determined to secure a place in India's squad for the 2027 ODI World Cup.In an interview with BCCI .tv after his match-winning innings, Rohit made it clear that outside speculation would not distract him from his responsibilities.“My job is with the bat. Come and play, represent my country, represent my team. That's what I have been told to do since my debut so that's what I am going to do,” Rohit said.“The noise since I made my debut was there. And till the time I am going to stay here, it is always going to be there. So it doesn't really matter too much. What matters is what I do on the field, try and contribute to the success of the team. That's all my focus is right now. And let the noise be there. If there is no noise, there is no fun.”Shukla also brushed aside calls for changes in India's leadership group following criticism directed at captain Shubman Gill and head coach Gautam Gambhir .“Everyone is entitled to their opinion, but the decision on who stays in the team and who does not rests with the selectors. The Indian team is performing well and winning matches, so there is no need for any changes at present,” Shukla said.Although Rohit's century at Lord's was one of the highlights of the tour, India finished the United Kingdom leg on a disappointing note. The visitors lost the ODI series against England 2-1 after earlier suffering a 2-0 defeat to Ireland and a 4-0 loss in the T20I series against England.
Article Summary: Bcci vice-president rajeev shukla has firmly rejected rumours over rohit sharma's international future. The 39-year-old became the first indian batter to score an odi century at lord's. Rohit has consistently maintained that he wants to continue representing the country.

Article Title: Underprepared East Bengal and Mohun Bagan kick-off new season with Durand Cup opener
Article Text:
Mohun Bagan vs East Bengal (PTI Photo)

KOLKATA: India’s oldest football tournament is hours away from an odd and unprecedented beginning. However, kick-starting the Durand Cup with a Kolkata derby for the first time in its 135th-year-old history has its own hype and hazards. Because, the blockbuster match between East Bengal FC and Mohun Bagan SG at the Salt Lake Stadium on Saturday will also set in motion the start of India’s domestic football season as well and the hard truth is that both teams look oddly underprepared.Let’s fix our gaze on some strange layers of the match. ISL champions East Bengal and runners-up Mohun Bagan — now under new coaches Antonio Lopez Habas and Panagiotis Dilmperis respectively — have hit the training ground running only four days ago.Not to mention the fact that while Habas will have only newcomer Dani Ramirez and old hand Mohammad Rashid available for selection, Dilmperis’ cupboard looks emptier with Serbian forward Dejan Drazic being the only foreigner to take part in Friday’s pre-match training session — a strange departure from the past when overseas players have predominantly emerged as show-stealers in such duels. It’s somewhat fitting that domestic players will now get the kind of spotlight they are rarely granted, thereby giving this season-opening derby primarily an indigenous spine."We haven't had enough time to train. It's impossible to prepare properly for such an important match in just a few days,” Habas admitted on Friday. "Our idea is to make the team solid, compact and competitive. We need time to develop our model of play, but that's the foundation we want to build," he added.It’s a strange but emotionally-charged homecoming for the 69-year-old Spaniard, who holds a rare link to the inaugural season of ISL and has guided now defunct ATK to two titles and Mohun Bagan to an ISL winner’s Shield.“I have absolute respect for Mohun Bagan and for everything we achieved together. I have wonderful memories of the fans and my time in Kolkata. But now I have another job, another responsibility. I have to fight for my new team," Habas said.His counterpart, Dilmperis — fondly called Panos — is also bracing for a challenging debut. Having made his mark as Punjab FC coach, the 51-year-old Greek couldn’t have asked for a toucher test for his coronation as Bagan coach.“Starting my journey with a derby is exciting because this is why football exists. Football is about rivalries, competition, and passion. Joining a club like Mohun Bagan, with its incredible fan base, rich history, ambitious ownership, and high expectations, is not pressure for me—it is a huge source of motivation," Panos remarked.“For me, every match is a derby. Whether we are playing the team at the top of the table or the bottom, I prepare with the same intensity,” he maintained.The last time a domestic tournament began with a derby happened way back in the 2004-2005 season of I-League. However, by that time, both teams had already gone through the grind of the local league.Starved of adequate time to pass muster, both teams are facing a whole new ball game. The likes of Bipin Singh, Edmund Lalrindika and David Lalhlansanga in the upfront as well as Jeakson Singh and Anwar Ali in defence contributed immensely to East Bengal’s march to the ISL summit last season. They will again be tasked with a new challenge of rising to the occasion.For Bagan, Liston Colaco, Manvir Singh and Sahal Abdul Samad will again be central to the team’s ambitions.However, it may threaten to float away into its own strange space; this season-opening derby with essentially a rare desi look will have the odds stacked against no team. It’s floating along the usual 50-50 narrative.
Article Summary: The durand cup kicks off with a kolkata derby for the first time in its 135th-year-old history. Isl champions east bengal and runners-up mohun bagan have hit the training ground running only four days ago. Both teams look oddly underprepared.

Article Title: India eye series win vs Zimbabwe: Can Abhishek Sharma break his lean run?
Article Text:
Abhishek Sharma (ANI Photo)

After the bruising their T20 side endured on the UK tour, this Zimbabwe series could be just the ideal fillip India needed.Having finally recorded their maiden win under new T20 captain Shreyas Iyer after seven winless matches at the helm, India will look to secure an unassailable 2-0 lead when they take on Zimbabwe in the second T20I at the Harare Sports Club on Saturday.Following a difficult run that saw them whitewashed by Ireland (0-2) and England (0-4), India’s convincing sevenwicket victory in the seriesopener has restored some much-needed confidence.Yet, even as the visitors look to build on that momentum, one player who will be under the scanner is explosive opener Abhishek Sharma.Two years ago, Harare was the venue where Abhishek announced himself on the international stage with a breathtaking maiden T20I hundred in only his second game.The stylish left-hander returns to the same ground searching for a spark after a worrying dip in form. Having begun the England series promisingly with scores of 59 and 43, Abhishek’s returns thereafter have read 10, 16, 3 and 1. In Thursday’s opener, his uncomfortable eight-ball 1 suggested a batter short on rhythm and confidence.With competition for places intensifying, Abhishek knows he needs runs. Senior opener Sanju Samson, though absent on this tour, remains in the selectors’ plans and has been named in India’s squad for the Asian Games later this year.A substantial score in Harare would not only help India seal the series but also strengthen Abhishek’s own case in a rapidly evolving T20 setup.India, though, found a new hero in the opening match.Teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashed a stunning 18-ball fifty, becoming the youngest player to score a T20I half-century.The 15-year-old, who had endured a difficult England tour where pacy bowlers like Jofra Archer tested him relentlessly with short-pitched bowling, responded in style against Zimbabwe.Taking on Richard Ngarava and Blessing Muzarabani fearlessly, he produced a blistering innings that underlined why he is so highly rated.Supported by Ishan Kishan’s brisk 35 and an unbeaten 28 from skipper Iyer, Sooryavanshi ensured India chased down the target with more than six overs to spare.Head coach VVS Laxman would have been equally pleased by the performance of India’s revamped pace attack. The biggest positive was the return of Mayank Yadav, who made an impressive comeback after two injury-ravaged years. The Delhi quick finished with figures of 2 for 18 and consistently touched high speeds, with his opening delivery to Brian Bennett at 150 kmph indidcating that his pace remains intact.Prince Yadav also showed signs of improvement after a lean England tour, while debutant Ashok Sharma displayed enough promise to suggest he could become another exciting fast-bowling option.
Article Summary: India will look to secure an unassailable 2-0 lead when they take on zimbabwe in the second t20i at the harare sports club on saturday. Abhishek sharma returns to the same ground searching for a spark after a worrying dip in form. Teenage sensation vaibhav sooryavanshi smashed a stunning 18-ball fifty.

Article Title: India's Sainyam settles for 10m pistol silver at Shooting World Cup in China
Article Text:
Sainyam

PUNE: Sainyam Vij missed the gold by just 0.2 points as she shrugged off multiple challenges from Olympic medallists, the world No. 1, her teammate and two local shooters at the ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou, China, on Friday.The Chandigarh girl clinched silver in the women’s 10m air pistol category after finishing behind reigning World No. 1 and World Champion shooter Qianxun Yao of China in the final.Sainyam scored 243.4 in the final, while Yao shot to gold with 243.6, while the bronze went to Iran’s Haniyeh Rostamiyan, who scored 221.On her way to the silver, Sainyam left Paris Games gold medallist Yejin Oh of Korea (8th), Tokyo Games double medallist Ranxin Jiang of China (5th) and her teammate Suruchi Phogat (7th) behind.“It was a good medal to win. I was not thinking about the field. For me the field was neither tough nor weak as I was focused on my own shooting,” Sainyam told TOI after winning the medal.
Article Summary: Sainyam vij missed the gold by just 0.2 points at the issf world cup in hangzhou, china. Chandigarh girl clinched silver in the women’s 10m air pistol category after finishing behind reigning world no. 1 and world champion qianxun yao of china.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit







El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El rubius was eliminated from mrbeast's $1 million challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

When the tickets get sold out, the demand gets too hig, and the cricket fans even ask for tickets in black. But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. In reply, CSK faltered under scoreboard pressure, with Sarfaraz Khan’s 50 off 24 balls and Prashant Veer’s 43 the lone acts of resistance amid a string of failures from the top order.Bhuvneshwar was at his disciplined best and even crossed the 200-mark in terms of wickets in IPL, with others also chipping in as CSK were bowled out for 207 in 19.4 overs. The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.
Article Summary: Royal challengers bengaluru (rcb) beat chennai super kings (csk) in ipl 2026 encounter at the m chinnaswamy stadium on sunday. Rcb register their second win over csk in the ipl. Tim david, rajat patidar and devdutt padikkal all scored half-centuries for rcb. Bhuvneshwar kumar took 3-41 to help rcb reach 250/3.

Article Title: Samurai quote of the day: 'You must understand that there is more than one path to the top of the mountain' and a timeless wisdom
Article Text:
Samurai quote of the day by Miyamoto Musashi

'You must understand that there is more than one path to the top of the mountain'

Meaning of the quote and the significance of the mountain

The samurai were the hereditary military nobility and warrior class of feudal Japan. Miyamoto Musashi was a Japanese swordsman, strategist, and philosopher born in the late sixteenth century. He is widely regarded as one of the most accomplished martial artists in history, having fought in over sixty duels without suffering a single defeat. His life spanned a transitional period in Japanese history, moving from the bloody civil wars of the Sengoku period into the long peace of the Tokugawa shogunate.Musashi began his career as a duelist at a very young age, killing his first opponent when he was just thirteen years old.As he traveled across Japan refining his skills, he eventually created his own unique style of fencing called Niten Ichi-ryu, which involved fighting with two swords simultaneously rather than holding a single blade with both hands. Later in life, Musashi withdrew from active combat to focus on painting, calligraphy, sculpture, and philosophy. Shortly before his death in a cave in 1645, he wrote down his life's philosophy in a text known as The Book of Five Rings.It is in this book that he wrote one of the greatest Samurai wisdom:There are many ways to do the same thing. And if all lead to success, the ways do not matter; the mountain matters. The quote about understanding that there is more than one path to the top of the mountain comes directly from Musashi's reflection on strategy, human growth, and spiritual discipline. At its core, the statement is a warning against dogmatic thinking and rigidity. Musashi believed that many people become overly attached to a single method, style, or set of rules, assuming that their chosen way is the only valid road to mastery.When applied to physical combat, the quote means that a true master must not rely on a single weapon or a single rigid fighting technique. A person who only knows how to use a single type of sword will fail when stripped of that sword. A strategist who insists on approaching every battle with the exact same tactic will inevitably be defeated by an opponent who can adapt. To Musashi, the ultimate goal of training was not to memorize specific moves, but to understand the universal nature of conflict and timing so deeply that one could succeed using any tool or approach available.Beyond martial arts, the metaphor of the mountain peak represents any ultimate goal, such as truth, self-mastery, personal success, or spiritual peace. The mountain peak remains fixed, but the routes up its sides are infinite. Some paths are steep and direct, requiring great physical strength. Other paths wind slowly around the slopes, relying on patience and endurance. Some routes require a person to navigate thick forests, while others demand climbing over open rock.Route vs destinationThe quote reminds us that the specific path a person takes is secondary to the actual climb. Two people can follow entirely different disciplines, rely on completely different life experiences, and hold different daily habits, yet both can achieve the exact same high level of wisdom and competence. Problems arise when people confuse the route for the destination. When someone becomes convinced that their specific path is the absolute only way to succeed, they often waste energy judging or opposing others who are simply climbing up a different side of the same mountain.Musashi observed this flaw frequently in the martial arts schools of his era. Many teachers claimed that their specific style was sacred and superior to all others. They taught fixed stances and ritualized movements that only worked in controlled environments. Musashi criticized this because it created a false sense of security. He argued that if a method does not work in a real, unpredictable situation, it is useless, no matter how prestigious its history might be.By encouraging people to look at the mountain rather than getting attached to one specific trail, Musashi promotes extreme adaptability. He advises individuals to remain flexible, open-minded, and pragmatic. If a chosen path becomes blocked by an unexpected landslide or cliff, an adaptable person does not sit down and give up, nor do they try to push through an impossible wall out of stubbornness. Instead, they simply step back, assess the terrain, and find a new way upward.Ultimately, the quote teaches self-reliance and broad perspective. It asks us to respect the diverse ways other people learn and grow, while encouraging us to find the specific approach that best fits our own nature and circumstances. Mastery is not about copying someone else's steps perfectly, but about reaching the summit through continuous effort, acute awareness, and unwavering resolve.
Article Summary: Miyamoto musashi was a japanese swordsman, strategist, and philosopher born in the late sixteenth century. He is widely regarded as one of the most accomplished martial artists in history, having fought in over sixty duels without suffering a single defeat. Musashi wrote down his life's philosophy in a text known as the book of five rings.

Article Title: Logitech G partners Call of Duty Modern Warfare 4: Here’s what users will get

Unique in-game items, including a Logitech G-themed weapon blueprint, weapon charm and calling card.

Community events, featuring in-game challenges, streamer events and other activities.

Signature hardware giveaways with Logitech G gaming gear.

"

The company also announced that its ASTRO Series will serve as the Official Headset Partner for the upcoming title.Announcing the partnership, Andrew Tagher, Head of Partnerships at Logitech G, said: "This partnership between Logitech G and Activision is about elevating & celebrating every player in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Article Title: 'I was really angry': Ex-India cricketer fumes over Rohit Sharma retirement saga
Article Text:
India's Rohit Sharma (ANI Photo)

Former India wicketkeeper Deep Dasgupta has criticised the speculation surrounding Rohit Sharma 's future during India's ODI series against England, saying the retirement rumours should never have gained traction while the team was still competing.The debate erupted after Rohit's early dismissal in the second ODI at Cardiff, with reports claiming the veteran opener would retire from ODIs after the series finale at Lord's. The report also suggested that the Indian team management was prepared to move on from the former captain because of his inconsistent form.The rumours gathered enough momentum for the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) to step in, with secretary Devajit Saikia dismissing the claims as baseless.Rohit responded in the best possible manner on the field. The opener smashed 138 off 110 balls in the third ODI at Lord's, although India eventually fell 27 runs short while chasing 388 and lost the three-match series 2-1.Reflecting on the episode, Dasgupta admitted he was frustrated by the discussions that dominated the series and questioned why such conversations had surfaced in the first place."I want to vent my anger a bit here because I was really angry when I was reading and listening to all of this.It is simple that as long as you keep scoring runs, you will keep playing. The only question comes in when that environment is created. Honestly, I have not heard it from any selector, captain, or the coach. It is a different matter if it was said off the field, which I am not privy to," he said on his YouTube channel.Following the conclusion of the series, Rohit also addressed the speculation in a video released by the BCCI, insisting that outside noise would not distract him from his responsibilities."What really matters is what I do on the field, try and contribute to the success of the team. That's where all my focus is. Let the noise be there, if there is no noise there is no fun. My job is inside, their job is outside, that's how I look at it," he said.India's next ODI assignment is a home series against the West Indies in September.Dasgupta also urged the selectors and team management to avoid creating unnecessary uncertainty around senior players such as Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli as India build towards the 2027 ODI World Cup.According to the former wicketkeeper, selection should continue to be based on performances rather than treating established stars differently."When you know that performances are needed, then these type of talks should not happen at all. Some people might get more chances, like Virat, Rohit, Shubman, they have been doing really well for years. It is not a debate about Rohit, it is a debate about everyone. When there are so many matches, it will happen, so just leave them alone. Don't treat them separately. Nothing has to change, just keep it simple," he concluded.
Article Summary: Deep dasgupta criticises speculation surrounding rohit sharma's future. Reports claimed the veteran opener would retire after the series finale at lord's. India lost the three-match odi series 2-1. The former wicketkeeper says selection should continue to be based on performances.

Article Title: World Cup gold-medallist rower fails dope test
Article Text: PUNE: In a major embarrassment for Indian rowing, and the Army Rowing Node (ARN) in particular, World Cup gold medallist Lakshay has been provisionally suspended after testing positive in an out-of-competition dope test.Lakshay, who combined with Ujjwal Singh to win the lightweight double sculls gold at World Cup III in Switzerland last month, tested positive for stanozolol in a sample collected in Pune on May 25.The triumph was India’s first-ever gold at a rowing World Cup. The result now stands to be annulled if the anti-doping violation is confirmed. The development is also a blow to India’s preparations for this year’s Asian Games, with the Lakshay-Ujjwal combination considered a medal prospect.The 23-year-old havildar from Haryana had won the lightweight double sculls gold with Ajay Tyagi at last year’s Asian Championships in Vietnam, where he was also part of the silver-winning quadruple sculls team.
Article Summary: Lakshay tested positive for stanozolol in an out-of-competition dope test. Lakshay combined with ujjwal singh to win the lightweight double sculls gold at world cup iii in switzerland. The triumph was india’s first-ever gold at a rowing world cup.

Article Title: 'Think about cricket, not social media': Ishan Kishan to Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
Article Text:
Ishan Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (AFP Photo)

NEW DELHI: India wicketkeeper-batter Ishan Kishan has backed teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, saying the 15-year-old has all the qualities to become a match-winner for the national team.Kishan'c comments came after India's 90-run win over Zimbabwe in the second T20I in Harare on Saturday. India were in early trouble after losing Abhishek Sharma (8) and Sooryavanshi (20) inside the first three overs, slipping to 29/2. Kishan then played a brilliant knock of 81 off 44 balls to guide India to 219/5. Zimbabwe were later bowled out for 129 as India sealed the three-match series 2-0 with one game to spare.Kishan said the senior members of the squad are helping Sooryavanshi settle into international cricket and are encouraging him to ignore distractions away from the game."Vaibhav is actually very smart. He knows what he is doing," Kishan said after India's win."He knows how he has to bat and how he has to carry himself on and off the field."The wicketkeeper-batter revealed that he, Abhishek Sharma, captain Axar Patel and other experienced players regularly speak to the youngster to ensure he remains focused."When you represent India, you have to know what to focus on," he said."Me, Abhishek, Axar bhai and many others keep telling him to think about cricket, not social media or outside noise."Kishan said the team wants Sooryavanshi to learn from the experiences of the senior players and avoid getting distracted early in his career."When you have such a player and you know that he is very young, you will never want him to be distracted for the wrong reasons."So our job as a team, we are like brothers and he comes from my place, so we just have to be happy, focus on the important things. The mistakes we have made in our starting, he should not do that. He should enjoy his cricket, like he is doing now."Kishan believes Sooryavanshi's attacking style can have a major impact on India's performances."If he stays on the pitch, the difference he can create for the team is huge. A player who can attack from the first ball can take you to 80-90 runs in the powerplay," he said.
Article Summary: India wicketkeeper-batter ishan kishan has backed teenage sensation vaibhav sooryavanshi. He said the 15-year-old has all the qualities to become a match-winner for the national team. The comments came after india's 90-run win over zimbabwe in the second t20i in harare.

Article Title: 'Gens Una Sumus' - What three Latin words beneath a chess emblem taught me about the world
Article Text:
(

Aarav Dengla

is India’s 93rd Grandmaster. He is a keen observer and student of the world history in general and chess history in particular)

My earliest memory of chess is from when I was seven years old.Walking into the venue of my first international tournament, my hand tucked inside my mother's, I stopped beneath the emblem of FIDE, the international federation governing chess. Three words, printed in a language I didn't understand, caught my eye.Gens Una Sumus.As I stood there trying to make sense of them, my mother gently squeezed my hand and reminded me that my game was about to begin.Afterwards, I found her waiting in a quiet corner of the dining area and asked what the words meant. She searched on her phone and told me they were Latin for: "We are one family."Since then, I have seen those words at tournaments across the world.Most players walk beneath them without noticing. I still do. They remind me that every time I enter a tournament hall, I am stepping into a community bound by shared values.Years later, I learned that the phrase predates modern chess by more than fifteen centuries. It comes from the Roman poet Claudian, whose words were later adopted by the chess world. Their meaning evolved - from describing one people to reminding us that, through chess, we become one family.That may sound like an ambitious motto for a sport. But after years of travelling to tournaments, I have come to believe it reflects the reality of chess.Chess is one of the few sports where almost anyone can compete on equal terms. You don't need expensive equipment or a particular physique. The board is the same in Reykjavik as it is in Chennai. Tournaments are held in grand hotels, school auditoriums and community halls, yet the rules never change. In most open events, anyone can enter.That means a child who learned the game only a few years earlier can be paired against someone who has spent decades playing it.I experienced that when I was eight years old in a town nestled in the Austrian Alps. My opponent was a man in his fifties. Our game lasted more than five hours and stretched well past midnight. The organisers waited patiently for us to finish because neither of us was willing to give up a square or agree to a draw.Across the board, age no longer mattered. Neither did reputation. There were only two players trying to solve the same position.Chess also brings people physically closer than most sports. We sit just across the board from each other for hours. We notice the slightest change in breathing, how long a hand hovers above a piece, the sudden stillness after a mistake, or the quiet confidence that follows a good move.Then the game ends. We shake hands. We reset the pieces.And more often than not, we sit down again - this time beside each other rather than opposite each other - to analyse what happened."I should have castled here.""No, I think the problem started earlier. Look at your knight."Only moments earlier, we were trying to outthink each other. Now we are trying to understand the game together.That has always fascinated me.Victory and defeat matter deeply while the clock is running. But once the clocks stop, curiosity usually takes over. Opponents become collaborators. Together, we search for the moment the game changed and help each other discover what we had both missed.Perhaps that is what Gens Una Sumus has come to mean to me.Chess does not erase differences. Tournament halls still contain rivalry, disappointment, ambition and, sometimes, genuine dislike. It is far from a perfect world.But it repeatedly places strangers across from one another and asks them to engage with respect. For a few hours, the person sitting opposite cannot be reduced to a nationality, an age, a rating or a stereotype. Every move demands that you take them seriously.When I first saw those three Latin words at the age of seven, I knew nothing about their history. I didn't know they had travelled across centuries before finding a home in the chess world.I only knew they made me stop.Today, after years of sitting across the board from people older and younger than me, from countries I had never visited and cultures I knew little about, I understand them differently.Every tournament begins with sixty-four squares.Many end with one more human connection.Gens Una Sumus.We are one family.
Article Summary: Chess is one of the few sports where almost anyone can compete on equal terms. Tournaments are held in grand hotels, school auditoriums and community halls. In most open events, anyone can enter. That means a child who learned the game only a few years earlier can be paired against someone who has spent decades playing it.

Article Title: 'What's his mistake?': Ex-India star wants India to make one big change for 3rd T20I vs Zimbabwe
Article Text:
BCCI Photo

NEW DELHI: Former India batter Aakash Chopra believes India should give Prabhsimran Singh a chance in the third and final T20I against Zimbabwe after already sealing the series. India have taken an unassailable 2-0 lead with convincing wins in the first two matches. The final game will be played in Harare on Sunday.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Chopra questioned why Prabhsimran has not been given an opportunity."I am thinking of playing Prabh (Prabhsimran Singh) as well. What's his mistake? You have selected Prabhsimran Singh, and we have no idea whatsoever when you would select him again.You have won the series," Chopra said.Chopra said India should continue backing Abhishek Sharma despite his poor scores in the first two matches. Instead, he suggested giving Ishan Kishan a break and bringing Prabhsimran into the playing XI. Abhished scored 1 run in the first T20I and then fell for 8 in the second T20I."So play him (Prabhsimran) in place of Abhishek, or else play him in place of Ishan. You can actually play him in place of Ishan.Don't play him in place of Abhishek. He hasn't scored runs. Two matches have gone badly for him. So play him the third as well. Make him score runs, and if a bowling option is required, make him do that job as well," the former opener said.Prabhsimran is yet to make his international debut. The Punjab Kings wicketkeeper-batter has scored 3,665 runs in 127 T20 innings at a strike rate of 151.50."Give a break to Ishan. Prabhsimran Singh will easily do the keeping job as well. So you can use him like that as a player. This is an opportunity that can be given to Prabh," he said.
Article Summary: Aakash chopra believes india should give prabhsimran singh a chance in the third and final t20i against zimbabwe. India have taken an unassailable 2-0 lead with convincing wins in the first two matches. The final game will be played in harare on sunday.

Article Title: Abhishek Sharma scripts history, enters Indian cricket's record books
Article Text:
India's Abhishek Sharma (AP Photo)

Tests: Vinoo Mankad – 8/52 vs Pakistan (1952)

ODIs: Ravi Shastri – 5/15 vs Australia (1991)

T20Is: Abhishek Sharma – 3/17 vs Zimbabwe (2026)

India all-rounder Abhishek Sharma etched his name into the record books after registering the best bowling figures by an Indian opener in T20I cricket during the second T20I against Zimbabwe on Saturday.The left-arm spinner returned figures of 3/17, surpassing every Indian opener to produce the finest bowling performance in the shortest format. His spell came as India thrashed Zimbabwe by 90 runs to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. Abhishek 's effort now sits alongside two iconic performances by Indian openers across formats. Vinoo Mankad continues to hold the record in Tests with his remarkable 8/52 against Pakistan in 1952, while Ravi Shastri's 5/15 against Australia in 1991 remains the best by an Indian opener in ODIs.Best bowling figures by an Indian opener:Abhishek had endured a disappointing outing with the bat after being dismissed cheaply by Blessing Muzarabani, but he made a decisive impact with the ball. Introduced as a part-time option, the left-arm spinner struck three times to ensure Zimbabwe never recovered during their daunting chase of 220.Zimbabwe's pursuit lost momentum after Brian Bennett's early aggression was cut short, and the visitors kept chipping away at regular intervals.Abhishek's three wickets, along with two each from Yash Thakur and Prince Yadav, bundled the hosts out for 129.Earlier, India recovered from 29/2 thanks to Ishan Kishan 's commanding 81 and Tilak Varma's unbeaten 60. Kishan steadied the innings before accelerating in the latter half of his knock, while Tilak produced a fluent half-century to power India to 219/5.The bowlers then completed the job in emphatic fashion, with Abhishek capping off the victory by creating a new Indian record.
Article Summary: India all-rounder abhishek sharma took 3/17 in the second t20i against zimbabwe. It is the best bowling figures by an indian opener in the shortest format. India thrashed zimbabwe by 90 runs to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the series.
